key_insight: Optimizing randomized Hamiltonian simulation for average-case error, rather than worst-case error, changes the best sampling rule from operator norms to Hilbert-Schmidt norms and can substantially reduce simulation error bounds.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical design rule for lower-depth quantum simulation circuits, especially when the target state is typical or when Pauli grouping is used to fit hardware constraints.
method: Model randomized Hamiltonian simulation as sequential short-time evolutions with arbitrary sampling probabilities.
Derive leading error bounds from the variance of sampled generators and optimize those bounds for either worst-case or Haar-averaged states.
Combine the average-error framework with commuting Pauli grouping to improve bounds at fixed $R_z$ depth.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports numerical benchmarks on the Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev model and the 108-qubit FeMoco Hamiltonian, including an approximately 5.65× reduction in error bounds for FeMoco.
watch_item: Average-error optimization is state-distribution dependent, so the improved sampling rule may not be ideal for adversarial or highly structured input states.
paper_title: Optimized Randomized Hamiltonian Simulation via Average-Error Analysis
